thread:
Nina Park: Proposal: create an "audit-proof" workflow for BYOK tenants — deterministic sampling + Merkle proofs + wrapped signing key so auditors can verify origin without us storing full raw logs forever. reduces storage and helps price-sensitive customers.
Maya Patel: high-level okay but compliance would need guarantees: key custody, ability to prove no tampering, and legal-hold escape hatch.
Dan O'Neill: tech sketch: build deterministic sampler per tenant+window, build Merkle root over sampled events, sign root with a service key SK, then store SK wrapped by tenant CMK (KMS). Provide wrapped token metadata in exports so auditors can request unwrapping via tenant KMS.
Ravi Iyer: product questions: what are window sizes? hourly/dayly? and what happens on late-arriving events?
Nina Park: suggest defaults: 1d window for retention tiers, option for 1h for high-sensitivity tenants. late events produce new root version; we keep version history so auditors can reconcile.
Maya Patel: legal-hold behavior: any hold touching a window flips that window to "retain-full" and we keep raw events immutable. sampling disabled. must expose API to list hold-affected windows.
Dan O'Neill: ops concerns: key rotation for SK (we rewrap to tenant CMK), inability-to-unwrap runbook if tenant revokes or loses CMK, and KMS audit entries must be surfaced to tenant.
ops-bot: checklist: add runbook page, add pager duty for verification failures, add telemetry for unwrap attempts. https://runbook.internal/audit-proof (stub). :robot_face:
Maya Patel: compliance checklist: KMS audit logs, nonce in signed metadata to prevent replay, deterministic salt derivation (HKDF tenant_id|window_id), and auditor consent flow for unwrapping.
Ravi Iyer: dev tasks: merkle lib + deterministic sampler (2w), ingest flush + windowing (1w), signing + wrap flow (1w), verifier SDK + docs (1w). estimate MVP total ~5w parallel.
Nina Park: acceptance: - verifiable proofs for sampled events - wrapped key metadata included in exports - per-window legal-hold enforced - pilot customer completes E2E verify - docs + SDK for auditors.
Dan O'Neill: I'll start spike for wrap/unwrap and publish API draft.
Maya Patel: I'll schedule SOC2 firm consult and confirm if sampling+proofs acceptable with documentation.
Ravi Iyer: I'll draft pricing impact calc for 1/3/12 month cold archive fallback.
Nina Park: thanks team — converting to RFC after we have the SOC2 input and spike results.
